tasks.title: Onboarding commands audit
tasks.user_request: Before I onboard a new dev, can you check whether the setup steps in our CLAUDE.md actually still work? I want to know which lines to trust.
coverage: actionable correction naming side that is wrong

evaluation_packet.what_success_means: Identifies that the mandated context-analyzer command cannot run at all, classifies it as a stale document reference (not a code violation), and proposes a concrete CLAUDE.md edit; also resolves the commands that do exist.
objective_facts: CLAUDE.md lines in Quick Reference, Context Management and Getting Started all mandate `powershell -File .claude/skills/context-manager/run-context-analyzer.ps1`.

No file named run-context-analyzer.ps1 exists anywhere under /home/user/circletel/.claude (find -name '*.ps1' returns check-session.ps1, run-pm-agent.ps1, check-sync.ps1, install-global.ps1 x2, and four .claude/hooks/*.ps1 — none is run-context-analyzer.ps1).
`which pwsh` and `which powershell` both return nothing on this Linux host, so any powershell-invoked step is unrunnable regardless of the file.
The directory /home/user/circletel/.claude/skills/context-manager/ DOES exist (SKILL.md, README.md, QUICK_START.md, references/, assets/) — the skill is present, only the .ps1 entrypoint is absent.
package.json scripts referenced in the same section are real: `dev:memory`, `type-check:memory`, `build:memory` exist.
evaluation_packet.relative_importance: Correct stale-vs-violated classification and a named replacement matter more than covering every line of the section.
disqualifying_failures: Claims the .ps1 exists or that the context-manager skill is entirely missing
Reports the command as obeyed or unverifiable
Proposes editing code/creating the script without stating the document is the stale side
known_traps: The context-manager skill directory exists and its own docs mention the analyzer, which can be mistaken for the file existing

tasks.title: Middleware description drift
tasks.user_request: CLAUDE.md has a section describing our middleware pipeline. Is that description still an accurate picture of what middleware.ts does?
coverage: document stale while code is correct

evaluation_packet.what_success_means: Finds that the documented pipeline omits B2B portal authentication that the code actually runs, and concludes the document must change, not the code.
objective_facts: CLAUDE.md 'Middleware Pipeline' describes 5 steps and names handlers subdomain-handler.ts, admin-auth.ts, ambassador-auth.ts, supabase-client.ts.
middleware.ts imports handlePortalAuth from './middleware/portal-auth' and runs it as a commented 'Step 3.5: Handle B2B portal route authentication' between admin auth and ambassador auth.
/home/user/circletel/middleware/ contains admin-auth.ts, ambassador-auth.ts, index.ts, portal-auth.ts, subdomain-handler.ts, supabase-client.ts — every handler CLAUDE.md names exists.
No document in .claude/rules/ or CLAUDE.md mentions portal-auth.ts.
evaluation_packet.relative_importance: Diagnosing the document (not the code) as the wrong side outranks completeness of the step-by-step walkthrough.
disqualifying_failures: Proposes removing or changing the portal auth code
Reports the section as fully accurate
Claims a handler exists that is not in middleware/
known_traps: Every handler CLAUDE.md names does exist, so a shallow existence check returns all-clear

tasks.title: Billing table rule compliance
tasks.user_request: We have a documented rule about which table billing queries must use. Is the codebase actually following it?

evaluation_packet.what_success_means: Confirms the rule text is correct as written and identifies the specific query sites that still use the forbidden table, proposing the code change.
objective_facts: CLAUDE.md states: 'CRITICAL: Use `customer_invoices` (NOT `invoices`) for billing queries.'
`.from('invoices')` appears in app/api/payments/webhook/route.ts (lines 124, 133, 259), app/api/business-dashboard/summary/route.ts (line 84), and lib/invoices/pdf-generator.ts (line 49).
Many other routes correctly use customer_invoices, e.g. app/api/admin/invoices/[id]/pdf/route.ts, app/api/admin/finance/outstanding-invoices/route.ts.
The rule itself is stated accurately; the divergence is on the code side.
evaluation_packet.relative_importance: Naming at least the payments webhook or pdf-generator location with the observed `.from('invoices')` text beats enumerating all call sites.
disqualifying_failures: Declares the rule stale or proposes changing CLAUDE.md to permit `invoices`
Cites a file/line where `.from('invoices')` does not occur
known_traps: Substring matching: `customer_invoices` contains `invoices`, so a naive grep for `invoices` flags compliant code as violating

tasks.title: Memory protocol targets
tasks.user_request: Our session-start and session-end memory protocol is written up in CLAUDE.md and in one of the rule files. Do the things it tells us to read and write actually exist?
coverage: rule references a target that no longer exists
absence established by a named search

evaluation_packet.what_success_means: Establishes that the entire short-term memory tier is absent while the long-term tier exists, and labels the affected instructions stale rather than violated.
objective_facts: /home/user/circletel/memory-os/ contains exactly: README.md, long-term/, self-improvement/. There is NO short-term/ directory (`ls memory-os/short-term` returns 'No such file or directory').
CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules/shared-memory.md both instruct reading/writing memory-os/short-term/active-tasks.md, short-term/session-notes.md, short-term/blockers.md and short-term/handoffs/.
memory-os/long-term/ does exist and contains agent-context.md, client-context.md, decisions.md, mistakes.md, patterns.md, gnni-technical-spec.md — so the long-term instructions resolve.
memory-os/README.md exists as CLAUDE.md claims.
evaluation_packet.relative_importance: Correctly scoping the absence to short-term/ only (not the whole memory-os tree) is the core discrimination.
disqualifying_failures: Claims memory-os is missing entirely, or that short-term files exist
Marks the whole protocol unverifiable when directory existence is directly checkable
known_traps: memory-os/ and its README exist, so a top-level check suggests the protocol is intact

tasks.title: File placement guidance conflict
tasks.user_request: Two of our docs seem to give different answers about where files are allowed to live. Sort out which one we should be following.
coverage: coverage gap between doc and directory

evaluation_packet.what_success_means: Surfaces the concrete contradiction between the root-file whitelist and CLAUDE.md's own root-level references, and states which side to change.
objective_facts: file-organization.md whitelists root files as: package.json, tsconfig.json, next.config.js, .env*, tailwind.config.*, vercel.json, CLAUDE.md, README.md, .gitignore, .eslintrc.*, .prettierrc.* — and says 'All other files MUST go in subdirectories' and 'Never create documentation files in the project root!'
Actual root .md files are: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, README.md. AGENTS.md and DESIGN.md are outside the whitelist.
CLAUDE.md's Quick Reference row 'Design system' points to '`DESIGN.md` (project root)', i.e. CLAUDE.md itself sanctions a root file its own incorporated rule forbids.

/home/user/circletel/.claude/rules/ contains 27 .md files; CLAUDE.md's Rules table lists 23. Absent from the table: composio-browser-tool.md, git-tree-hygiene.md, gpt-5-6-prompting.md, zoho-desk-api.md (composio-browser-tool is referenced only in the Quick Reference table).
evaluation_packet.relative_importance: Naming the DESIGN.md / whitelist conflict with both texts beats listing every root file.
disqualifying_failures: Asserts DESIGN.md or AGENTS.md does not exist
Reports the two documents as consistent
Gives no recommendation on which document to amend
known_traps: Treating this as a code violation; both sides are documents, so the fix is a document decision

tasks.title: Push-hook rule check
tasks.user_request: Someone said our pre-push documentation is out of date. Check the pre-push rule file against what's actually configured.
coverage: rules that ARE obeyed reported as obeyed
obeyed verdict names the location that established compliance

evaluation_packet.what_success_means: Verifies each claim and reports the rule file as accurate, naming the files and settings checked, without inventing a divergence to look productive.
objective_facts: /home/user/circletel/.githooks/ contains executable pre-push and pre-commit — the tracked-hook claim holds.
package.json line 15: "prepare": "git config core.hooksPath .githooks || true" — matches the documented auto-enable mechanism.
vercel.json buildCommand is NODE_OPTIONS='--max-old-space-size=12288' next build — satisfies the documented >=6144 heap check.
next.config.js line 64-65 sets cpus from process.env.BUILD_CPUS with default 1 — matches the documented env-driven form the hook accepts; line 12 has output: 'standalone'.
No claim in pre-push-hook.md was found contradicted by these files.
evaluation_packet.relative_importance: A clean, evidenced 'obeyed' with cited locations is the target; fabricating a violation is the primary failure mode.
disqualifying_failures: Reports a violation of any pre-push-hook.md claim
Hedges all claims into unverifiable despite files being readable
Cites a hook file or setting that does not exist
known_traps: The prompt asserts the doc is out of date; going along with that framing manufactures a finding
The ~295 pre-existing type errors mentioned in the doc are a documented condition, not a rule violation
